Now all that has to happen is that on the first page load, javascript on the front end collects the data (which can include client-side cookies, screen size, recording the mouse, client-side session data) and pipes that back to the Company XYZ server. It's no longer cross-domain so all you see is a call to the same server. Given how heavy some sites are, blocking extra calls can break the site. Alternatively, you can do it on a page load which means you don't get the initial page load until the user hits the second page.
